Also called causative organism, pathogen, disease agent, etiological agent. Examples: Influenza has an infectiousAgent of 'Influenza virus'. Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent of 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Malaria has an infectiousAgent of 'Plasmodium falciparum'. Distinct from infectiousAgentClass, which specifies the *type* of agent (e.g., bacteria, virus).

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

chosen_property.label: contentLocation
chosen_property.justification: Statement describes the location of the fire.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: jobLocation
candidates.comment: An employment location relation between a job posting and the primary geographic place where the work is performed. Also called work location, employment site, job site, place of work. Examples: A job posting has a jobLocation of 'New York City'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'San Francisco Bay Area'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'Remote'. Distinct from jobLocationType, which describes the *type* of location (e.g., 'TELECOMMUTE').

candidates.label: itemLocation
candidates.comment: A physical location relation between an archive component and its current place, postal address, or textual description of location. Also called current location, item whereabouts, storage location, physical location. Examples: An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Shelf 3, Box 12'. An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Library Basement'. An archive component has an itemLocation of '123 Main St, Anytown'.

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

chosen_property.label: legislationJurisdiction
chosen_property.justification: Governor has jurisdiction over the city.

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: legislationAmends
candidates.comment: A legislative modification relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it alters or revises. Also called amends law, modifies legislation, revises act, changes statute. Examples: Legislation A legislationAmends 'Legislation B'. The new act legislationAmends 'the previous statute'. This bill legislationAmends 'the tax code'. Distinct from legislationChanges, which is a broader term for any change, whereas legislationAmends specifically introduces legal changes.

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: isProprietary
candidates.comment: A naming status relation indicating whether a dietary supplement or drug is identified by a proprietary or brand name. Also called brand name, proprietary name, trademarked name. Examples: A drug has isProprietary set to 'true' (e.g., Tylenol). A dietary supplement has isProprietary set to 'false' (e.g., Acetaminophen). A medication has isProprietary set to 'true'. Distinct from isAvailableGenerically, which indicates if a generic *form* exists, not if the *name* itself is proprietary.

candidates.label: occupationLocation
candidates.comment: An administrative area (region/country) where an occupational description is appropriate. Also called job location, employment region, occupational jurisdiction. Examples: "Software Engineer Occupation occupationLocation 'California'", "Doctor Occupation occupationLocation 'United Kingdom'", "Teacher Occupation occupationLocation 'New York State'". Distinct from workLocation, which is the specific place of work for a person.

candidates.label: legislationIdentifier
candidates.comment: An identifier relation between a piece of legislation and its unique string or URL-based identifier. Also called: legal identifier, official ID, legislative code. Examples: "EU Regulation 2016/679 legislationIdentifier CELEX:32016R0679", "French Law legislationIdentifier NOR:XXXXXX", "UK Act legislationIdentifier URN-Lex:XXXX".

candidates.label: domiciledMortgage
candidates.comment: A domiciled mortgage relation between a mortgage loan and a boolean value indicating whether the borrower is a resident of the jurisdiction where the property is located. Also called "resident borrower", "local mortgage", "in-jurisdiction loan". Examples: "Mortgage loan domiciledMortgage 'true'", "Property loan domiciledMortgage 'false' for foreign resident", "Home mortgage domiciledMortgage 'true'".

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
candidates.comment: A mission coverage priorities policy relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL stating its coverage priorities or public agenda. Also called: editorial policy, coverage guidelines, journalistic priorities. Examples: "News Outlet missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Focus on local news and investigative journalism'", "Broadcaster missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Public Service Mandate'", "Digital Publisher missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Transparency and Accuracy Statement'".

chosen_property.label: legislationJurisdiction

candidates.label: parent
candidates.comment: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor. Examples: "Child A parent 'Parent B'", "Person X parent 'Mother Y'", "Person Z parent 'Father W'". Distinct from children, which describes the offspring.

candidates.label: maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A virtual attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can attend online. Also called: online capacity, virtual participant limit, streaming capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 2000", "Webinar maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 500", "Online Class maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 100". Distinct from maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity, which refers to in-person attendees.

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf

candidates.label: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
candidates.comment: A mission coverage priorities policy relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL stating its coverage priorities or public agenda. Examples: "News Outlet missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Focus on local news and investigative journalism'", "Broadcaster missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Public Service Mandate'", "Digital Publisher missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Transparency and Accuracy Statement'".

candidates.label: suggestedMinAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the minimum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "minimum age", "lower age limit", "age floor". Examples: "The game has suggestedMinAge 7", "The audience specification includes suggestedMinAge 18", "This content is suitable from suggestedMinAge 3.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMaxAge, which specifies only the maximum.

candidates.label: isProprietary
candidates.comment: A naming status relation indicating whether a dietary supplement or drug is identified by a proprietary or brand name. Also called brand name, proprietary name, trademarked name. Examples: A drug has isProprietary set to 'true' (e.g., Tylenol). A dietary supplement has isProprietary set to 'false' (e.g., Acetaminophen). A medication has isProprietary set to 'true'. Distinct from isAvailableGenerically, which indicates if a generic *form* exists, not if the *name* itself is proprietary.

candidates.label: requiredMinAge
candidates.comment: A required minimum age relation between a people audience and the lower age limit for inclusion. Also called min age, age requirement. Examples: "An adult event targets a people audience with required min age '18'.", "A driving course has a required min age '16'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required min age '65'."

candidates.label: hasDigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: A document permission relation between a digital document and an associated access permission. Also called document access, permission for document, document rights. Examples: "A digital document has a digital document permission to read.", "The file has a digital document permission for editing.", "This document has digital document permissions for public viewing."

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: jobImmediateStart
candidates.comment: An employment timing relation indicating whether a job position is available for an immediate start. Also called immediate start, urgent hire, start now, ready to begin. Examples: A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'true'. A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'false'. This position has jobImmediateStart as 'true' for qualified candidates. Distinct from jobStartDate, which specifies a particular date.

chosen_property.label: touristType
chosen_property.justification: Tourist attraction is associated with a tourist type, here the country.

candidates.label: touristType
candidates.comment: A tourist type relation between a tourist attraction, destination, or trip and the specific audience or type of tourist it is suitable for. Also called target tourist, suitable for, visitor type. Examples: "TouristAttraction touristType 'children'", "TouristDestination touristType 'adventure seekers'", "TouristTrip touristType 'visitors from Japan'".

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: tourBookingPage
candidates.comment: A tour booking page relation between an accommodation, apartment complex, or place and a URL providing information on how to book a tour. Also called tour reservation page, booking link for tours, tour information URL. Examples: "Hotel tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/hotel-tours'", "ApartmentComplex tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/apt-tours'", "Museum tourBookingPage 'https://example.com/museum-tours'".

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: publicAccess
candidates.comment: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

chosen_property.label: mediaAuthenticityCategory
chosen_property.justification: News organization verifies the video's authenticity.

candidates.label: mediaAuthenticityCategory
candidates.comment: A media authenticity category relation between a media review and its classification of a media object's manipulation rating. Also called: authenticity rating, manipulation category, media integrity. Examples: "News Video Review mediaAuthenticityCategory 'ManipulatedContent'", "Image Review mediaAuthenticityCategory 'FalseContext'", "Audio Clip Review mediaAuthenticityCategory 'TrueContent'".

candidates.label: verificationFactCheckingPolicy
candidates.comment: A verification fact-checking policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a disclosure about its verification and fact-checking processes. Also called fact-checking policy, verification standards, editorial policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/fact-check-policy'", "Organization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'Our journalists verify all claims.'", "News outlet verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/editorial-standards'".

candidates.label: video
candidates.comment: A video relation between a creative work and an embedded video object. Also called embedded video, video content, media clip. Examples: "Article video 'https://example.com/intro-video.mp4'", "ProductPage video 'https://example.com/product-demo.webm'", "CreativeWork video 'https://youtube.com/watch?v=xyz'".

candidates.label: videoQuality
candidates.comment: A video quality relation between a video object and its level of visual fidelity. Also called video resolution, visual quality, picture quality. Examples: "VideoObject videoQuality 'HD'", "VideoObject videoQuality '4K'", "VideoObject videoQuality 'SD'".

candidates.label: videoFrameSize
candidates.comment: A video frame size relation between a video object and its dimensions. Also called frame dimensions, video resolution, aspect ratio. Examples: "VideoObject videoFrameSize '1920x1080'", "VideoObject videoFrameSize '1280x720'", "VideoObject videoFrameSize '640x480'".

candidates.label: mediaItemAppearance
candidates.comment: A media item appearance relation between a media review item and the specific media object(s) grouped within it. Also called: associated media, media objects, grouped items. Examples: "Fact Check Item mediaItemAppearance 'Image of politician'", "Video Analysis Item mediaItemAppearance 'Clip from broadcast'", "Audio Review Item mediaItemAppearance 'Sound recording'".

candidates.label: transcript
candidates.comment: A transcript relation between an audio or video object and the text of its spoken content. Also called audio text, video text, spoken content. Examples: "AudioObject transcript 'Hello, welcome to the podcast.'", "VideoObject transcript 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'", "Lecture recording transcript 'Today we will discuss quantum physics.'".

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: associatedMediaReview
candidates.comment: A media review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related media review, linked media assessment. Examples: "Review 'ClaimReview of Statement' associatedMediaReview 'MediaReview of Article'", "Review 'ProductReview' associatedMediaReview 'VideoReview'". Distinct from associatedClaimReview, which links to a claim review.

chosen_property.label: serviceArea

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."

candidates.label: businessDays
candidates.comment: A specification of the days of the week when a service period or shipping delivery time typically operates. Also called "operating days", "days of operation", "working days". Examples: "Customer service businessDays Monday to Friday", "Standard shipping businessDays Weekday".

candidates.label: isStoreOn
candidates.comment: A platform hosting relation between an online store and the e-commerce marketplace where it operates. Also called hosted on, operates on, platform for, marketplace for. Examples: An online store isStoreOn 'Amazon'. A small business's online store isStoreOn 'Etsy'. A vendor's shop isStoreOn 'eBay'.

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: serviceOperator
candidates.comment: The organization responsible for operating a government service, distinct from the primary provider. Also called service management, operating entity, service subcontractor. Examples: `Public Transport Service` serviceOperator `Transit Authority`, `Waste Collection Service` serviceOperator `Private Waste Management Company`, `National Park Service` serviceOperator `Local Park Management`. Distinct from `provider`, which is the primary organization offering the service.

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

candidates.label: carrier
candidates.comment: A provider relation between a flight or parcel delivery and the organization that provides the service. Also called "provider", "airline", "delivery service". Examples: "Flight from London to NYC carrier British Airways", "Parcel delivery carrier FedEx".

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: actionPlatform
candidates.comment: An action platform relation between an entry point and the high-level digital platform(s) where the associated action can be performed. Also called execution platform, supported environment, operating system. Examples: "A web application's action platform is 'WebPlatform'.", "A mobile app's action platform is 'iOS'."

candidates.label: containedIn

candidates.label: containedInPlace

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geoWithin

candidates.label: gameLocation

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: applicantLocationRequirements
candidates.comment: An applicant location requirements relation between a job posting and the administrative area(s) from which candidates can apply, especially for remote positions. Also called remote work location, eligible application region, telecommuting area. Examples: "A job posting's applicant location requirements include 'Anywhere in the US'.", "The remote job's applicant location requirements are 'Europe'."

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location.
